name: The Ash Remembers
storyline:
Ash has been falling over Veyr for as long as the chronicles reach. It settles on roofs, on roads and on the names of the dead, and it forgets nothing — while the embers beneath it go on glowing, patient and awake.

Through the gates of the city of Emberwake comes a stranger the townspeople call the Wanderer. The Wanderer does not remember why they are there. The city, however, saw them coming long before they found the gates.

There is no prophecy here and no chosen one. The Wanderer mines, forges, fishes, cooks and fights, builds a standing in a place that was never waiting to be saved, and eventually walks out to meet the things that stand at the edge of the ash: world bosses, weekly titans, and finally the reason the ash remembers at all.

When there is nothing left to gain, the Ashfall offers the only thing the world has ever offered anyone — the chance to let everything go and begin again, carrying nothing but what was learned.
summary:
The Ash Remembers is a dark fantasy idle RPG set in Veyr, a world where ash has been falling for as long as the chronicles reach — and where the ash does not forget. The player arrives at the city of Emberwake as a nameless wanderer and builds a life there: fighting, gathering, cooking and forging.

Progress continues while the game is closed. Combat, gathering and crafting run offline, so a returning player finds work already done instead of a backlog to catch up on.

Sixteen professions feed into one another. Mining and smelting supply the forge, farming and fishing supply the kitchen, and cooked food is what keeps a character standing in long fights — there is no pure-combat path through the game.

More than 120 enemies, eight weekly titans and a line of world bosses make up the endgame. Each carries its own damage weakness, loot table and piece of story, and matching a weapon to that weakness matters more than raw numbers. The Ashfall lets a character let go of everything and begin again stronger: the world's own form of prestige, and never a resurrection.

The game is menu- and text-driven rather than action-driven, runs in the browser and as a desktop build, and is fully playable in German and English. It tells no chosen-one story — nobody here is saving the world, and the chronicle never claims otherwise.
